name: Discriminating Cases
description: Shows that a solution's cases can actually fail, which is the only evidence a measure has when the solution has no rival to compare against.
purpose: Prove that a solution's cases can tell a sound implementation from a naive one, even when only one implementation exists.
approach: Write deliberately naive implementations and show that each one fails the cases.
out_of_scope: Inventing rivals that exist only to lose a comparison.
milestones: 1. Case discrimination: a recorded run of the share of solutions whose naive baselines all fail their cases.
knowledge: Mutation testing; the gap between a passing test and a meaningful one.
measures_of_success: No case set passes everything that is put in front of it. Standing conditions: Every invariant solution has at least one naive baseline that fails its cases.
inputs: A solution's cases and its naive baselines.
outputs: A pass or fail per baseline.
usage_notes: Write the naive version a first draft would produce, not a deliberately silly one.
